system_description.narrative_title: Fragmentation, Shock and Acceleration in a Tech- and Energy-Driven Order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system strained by simultaneous shocks: a tech-governance crisis around frontier AI, an energy-security shock from Middle East maritime and pipeline attacks, and financial stress as inflation and higher yields force central banks toward tighter policy. These dynamics interact through feedback loops—energy disruptions raise inflation and borrowing costs, which amplify market volatility and political pressure, while rapid AI advances provoke regulatory battles and geopolitical competition that reshape alliances and corporate strategies. The system is therefore in flux: short-term crisis management (shipping, markets, conflict containment) sits atop longer-term structural shifts (BRICS expansion, supply-chain realignment, tech governance).
system_description.scope: Nation-states, multinational corporations (notably tech and energy firms), global financial markets and central banks, international institutions (NATO, IEA, IAEA, BRICS), critical infrastructure and supply routes (shipping lanes, pipelines), and public/political opinion across major powers.
system_description.super_system: The global socio-political-economic system (the international order encompassing geopolitics, world markets, and transnational governance)

variables.name: Middle East maritime chokepoints and spillover
variables.description: Iran, Gulf states (including Saudi Arabia and the UAE), Iran-backed Houthi forces and the U.S. are engaged in a widening conflict that is shifting risk onto strategic sea lanes and energy export routes, disrupting global oil flows and shipping security.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine kinetic escalation and NATO friction
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with growing involvement from NATO members and neighbouring states, are experiencing renewed kinetic escalation—including cross-border strikes and drone use—that is shifting battlefield dynamics and intensifying alliance security tensions.

variables.name: AI development, safety and governance contest
variables.description: Major AI firms and regulators—primarily U.S. industry players, U.S. and allied governments, and China—are locked in a contested debate over slowing frontier model development and new safety rules, shifting norms about acceptable pace, oversight and national-security uses of advanced AI.

variables.name: Global monetary repricing and bond-market stress
variables.description: The U.S. Federal Reserve, other central banks and global investors are driving a rapid repricing of interest rates and risk (with U.S. yields spiking), shifting capital flows, borrowing costs and policy calculations worldwide.

variables.name: Tech, trade and supply‑chain decoupling
variables.description: The U.S., China and other major economies are accelerating industrial policy, export controls and investment shifts around semiconductors, data infrastructure and strategic technologies, shifting the contours of global supply chains and economic interdependence.
